### Steps to reproduce

```bash
uv build --project packages/server   # at tag 0.4.0-rc1
pip install memmachine_server-0.4.0rc1-py3-none-any.whl
python -c "import memmachine_server.retrieval_agent.agents.rarag_query_agent"
# ERROR Decomposer import FAILED + traceback (same on memmachine-server startup)
```

### Expected behavior

An optional dependency that is absent by design logs one INFO/WARNING line, such as "multi-hop decomposer disabled; install with `uv sync --group multihop`", not an ERROR with a traceback.

### Environment

- MemMachine Version: 0.4.0-rc1 (`ad8ff24`)
- OS: Ubuntu, Python 3.12

items.body:
### Severity: Medium
**Layer:** CICD
**Location:** `.github/workflows/ci.yml:16` (`pip install -e . && pip install pytest`), `pyproject.toml:24-25` (pyyaml lives only in the `full`/`dev` extras), `tests/test_config.py:27`, `tests/test_deceive.py:85`

### Reproduction (verified)
The workflow installs the base package only: `pip install -e .` pulls `dependencies = []` — PyYAML is never installed. In a clean venv mirroring CI (`pip install -e .` + `pip install pytest`), running the CI command `python3 -m pytest tests/ -q` fails:

```
FAILED tests/test_config.py::TestConfig::test_yaml_config_merge
FAILED tests/test_deceive.py::TestDeceptionGrid::test_save_and_load_yaml
2 failed, 98 passed
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'yaml'
```

`test_yaml_config_merge` and `test_save_and_load_yaml` both `import yaml` at runtime.

### Expected vs actual
- Expected: the README badge (`README.md:7`) shows tests green on `main`.
- Actual: every push/PR to `main` runs a red workflow; the YAML config/`grid.yaml` paths are never exercised in CI.

The README Quickstart (`README.md:94`) installs `".[full]"` — only the CI job omits the extra.

### Safe remediation
1. In CI, replace `pip install -e .` with `pip install -e ".[full]"` (lowest risk, matches documented Quickstart and adds `pyyaml>=6.0`).
2. Optionally add a `pip check` step so dependency drift fails loudly.

items.title: [Bug]: tools/neutts_synth.py discards the real exception on a failed neutts import, always prints the same hardcoded message
items.body:
## Bug Description
`tools/neutts_synth.py` catches `ImportError` when loading the `neutts` package and always prints a hardcoded "not installed" message, discarding the real exception text. `except ImportError` also fires for a *transitive* dependency failure inside neutts's own import chain (e.g. a torch/numpy native library failing to load under resource contention) — not just a genuinely-missing package — so the hardcoded message actively misleads whoever's debugging a transient failure into thinking they need to reinstall a package that's already installed.

## Steps to Reproduce
1. Get `neutts` into a state where its own transitive import chain fails at runtime for a reason other than "not installed" (e.g. a native library load failure under CPU/disk contention from other concurrently-running processes).
2. Run `tools/neutts_synth.py`.
3. Read the printed error.

## Expected Behavior
The error message should include the real exception text, so a transient dependency-load failure is distinguishable from a genuinely-missing package.

## Actual Behavior
The message is always the same hardcoded string ("neutts not installed. Run: python -m pip install -U neutts[all]") regardless of the actual cause. Confirmed live: two separate production failures on the same install were both this exact message with the real underlying exception silently discarded, making it impossible after the fact to tell "genuinely not installed" from "transient failure loading a real dependency."

## Affected Component
- [x] Tools (terminal, file ops, web, code execution, etc.)

## Root Cause Analysis
```python
except ImportError:
    print("Error: neutts not installed. Run: python -m pip install -U neutts[all]", file=sys.stderr)
```
`str(e)` was always available here and simply never printed.

## Proposed Fix
```python
except ImportError as e:
    print(f"Error: neutts import failed ({e}). If genuinely not installed, "
          f"run: python -m pip install -U neutts[all]", file=sys.stderr)
```

We have this applied as a local patch and are happy to open the PR ourselves.

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS

3.11.15 (hermes-agent venv)

items.title: Unchanged tests give no credit to the module they import, and the missing-module hint says to pip-install the project's own package

labels.name: area/proxy
labels.description: Go agent loop and SSE contract (proxy/)

items.body:
## What happens
- When a session changes a module and runs the project's existing
  tests, the run is not counted as evidence for the change: test
  discovery and the import walk only look at files the session
  itself changed. A correct change can then end as "verification
  demanded, not met". Go projects already work.
- When a Python import fails for a module that lives in the
  workspace, the hint says the package is not installed and suggests
  `pip install`. The install fails, because the module is the
  project's own. A project with only `pyproject.toml` or a `Pipfile`
  gets `pip install -r requirements.txt`.

## What needs doing
- An unchanged test that the runner discovered is a way in: it is
  followed through real imports (a few hops, no credit for ambiguous
  names) to the changed files it covers. It is never itself counted
  as covered.
- The hint looks for the module in the workspace first and gives
  path or project-root advice for local names. Install advice stays
  for third-party names.

## Done when
- [ ] A change covered only by an existing, unchanged test is
  credited, for pytest, unittest and the common JavaScript runners.
- [ ] Running one test file no longer credits an unrelated changed
  file.
- [ ] A failed import of a workspace module gets no install advice.

items.title: [Feature]: Installer resilience improvements for GitHub-restricted networks (mainland China) - stale script cache, no mirror fallback, misleading recovery hints

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

labels.name: sweeper:risk-platform-windows
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break or behave differently on native Windows

items.body:
## Problem or Use Case

I just completed an install/upgrade of Hermes on a Chinese-locale Windows machine behind GitHub-restricted networking. The install only succeeded after manual intervention at **five** separate points; each one would silently fail or loop forever for a user who doesn't read the bootstrap log. Full failure chain:

**1. Stale cached bootstrap script → `INSTALL DIDN'T FINISH: Baseline imports failed` (the headline symptom)**

- `bootstrap-cache/install-main.ps1` was cached ~6 weeks earlier and never refreshed (log: `using cached install.ps1 for main`).
- That old script pinned the venv to **Python 3.11**, while `pyproject.toml` gates *every* core dependency behind `; python_version >= '3.14'` (changed on main 2026-09-27).
- Result: `uv pip install -e ".[all]"` against the 3.11 venv **silently skipped every gated dependency** (`openai`, `python-dotenv`, `rich`, `prompt_toolkit`, …) — 61 packages installed, zero core deps — and only then did the baseline import gate fail:
  `Baseline imports failed in <install-dir>\venv (dotenv/openai/rich/prompt_toolkit)`
- **Retrying could never work**: the stale cache was never invalidated, so every retry replayed the identical failure. I had to delete the cached script by hand to force a fresh download.

**2. Missing `uv.lock` disabled the verified tier, and the suggested recovery command cannot work**

- With `uv.lock` absent from the worktree the installer logs `uv.lock not found -- falling back to PyPI resolve (no hash verification)` and drops to plain `uv pip install`.
- The failure dialog then suggests: `Recover with: … uv sync --extra all --locked` — which **cannot succeed without the lockfile** (and would fail on the 3.11 venv anyway, since the lock only covers `python_version >= '3.14'`). Recovery hints should be validated before they are shown.

**3. `raw.githubusercontent.com` fetch has no mirror/proxy fallback**

- The bootstrap's own script download failed twice: `resolve install script failed: GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/… (os error 10054, connection reset)`.
- Notably, `git fetch` inside the same installer already succeeds through a mirror (configured via `insteadOf`), but the HTTP downloader has no equivalent fallback. My workaround was copying `scripts/install.ps1` from a local clone into `bootstrap-cache/install-main.ps1` by hand.

**4. pm tool unpack: transient `WinError 5` kills the whole `python-deps` stage**

- Installing the managed CPython distribution failed moving `tree\python\DLLs -> tree\DLLs` with `[WinError 5] Access is denied` — a transient lock on freshly extracted DLLs (almost certainly antivirus scanning; the same rename succeeded manually minutes later, and the stage succeeded on the next full run).
- The internal retry gave up after 2 attempts within ~15 s and failed the entire stage. Backoff should be longer/exponential for rename-after-extract, and the message should distinguish "file in use" from a real ACL problem.

**5. `products` stage: Electron + electron-builder toolsets download straight from GitHub Releases**

- `electron-v40.10.2-win32-x64.zip` (138 MB) stalled at 4–33% across attempts, then `TypeError: fetch failed`; `icons-bundle.tar.gz`, 7zip, and the winCodeSign kit (ATS dlib, .NET runtime, Windows SDK, rcedit) all come from the same host.
- Setting the standard ecosystem mirrors completed **all** downloads in ~3 minutes:
  - `ELECTRON_MIRROR=https://npmmirror.com/mirrors/electron/`
  - `ELECTRON_BUILDER_BINARIES_MIRROR=https://npmmirror.com/mirrors/electron-builder-binaries/`

### Sanitized log excerpts

```
[bootstrap] using cached install.ps1 for main
-> uv.lock not found -- falling back to PyPI resolve (no hash verification)
{"ok":false,"stage":"dependencies","reason":"Baseline imports failed in <install-dir>\\venv (dotenv/openai/rich/prompt_toolkit). … Recover with: … uv sync --extra all --locked"}
[bootstrap] downloading install.ps1 for mutable ref main from GitHub
ERROR resolve install script failed: GET https://raw.githubusercontent.com/… (os error 10054)
[X] python: install failed: [WinError 5] … '…\.staging-xxx\tree\python\DLLs' -> '…\tree\DLLs' … retry, or run `hermes pm doctor`
downloading label=electron progress=6%   (repeated, then)   TypeError: fetch failed
```

## Proposed Solution

1. **Invalidate the cached install script** (TTL / conditional request / pin it to the fetched commit) so an old script can never pair with a newer `pyproject.toml`. At minimum, warn when the cached script is older than N days.
2. **Fail fast on version mismatch**: before installing, verify the venv interpreter satisfies the dependency markers of the checked-out `pyproject.toml` (e.g. core deps are 3.14-gated while the venv is 3.11) and print an actionable error — instead of "Baseline imports failed" after a green-looking install.
3. **Mirror-aware downloads with automatic fallback**: honor `ELECTRON_MIRROR` / `ELECTRON_BUILDER_BINARIES_MIRROR` (already standard in the Electron ecosystem) and add an equivalent fallback for `raw.githubusercontent.com` requests (mirror list or a `HERMES_DOWNLOAD_MIRROR` knob), mirroring what git already does via `insteadOf`. Consider auto-falling back to a known mirror after repeated 10054/10060 connection resets.
4. **Validate recovery hints**: never suggest `uv sync --locked` when `uv.lock` is absent — suggest restoring it first (`git checkout -- uv.lock`) or omit the `--locked` tier explanation.
5. **Exponential backoff** for `WinError 5` / sharing-violation retries right after extraction; don't fail the whole stage after two quick attempts.
6. **Document the mirror environment variables** in the Windows install/troubleshooting docs.

I'm happy to re-test any fix on this network environment.

## Alternatives Considered

- **Require users to configure a system proxy**: unrealistic for most users in this region; the installer already works around this for git, so the HTTP paths should be consistent.
- **Ship a full offline bundle**: large maintenance burden; automatic mirror fallback is smaller and benefits every restricted-network user (not just China).

## Feature Type

- Performance / reliability

## Scope

- Medium (few files, < 300 lines)

items.body:
The latest stable release (2026.7.20) no longer displays any `Structure` or `Molecule` in Jupyter for a fresh install. I would like a stable PyPI release that fixes both of the problems below, so that my pymatgen and atomate2 tutorials can go back to a plain `pip install crystal-toolkit`.

Repro in a fresh environment (a fresh `pip install crystal-toolkit jupyter` today gives crystal-toolkit 2026.7.20, pymatgen 2026.9.24 / pymatgen-core 2026.9.23, flask-caching 2.5.1, dash 3.4.0; tested on Python 3.12 with JupyterLab 4.6.4):
```python
import crystal_toolkit
from pymatgen.core import Lattice, Structure
Structure(Lattice.cubic(3.9), ["Pb"], [[0, 0, 0]])  # last line of a notebook cell
```

1. **pymatgen >= 2026.9.23 removed `StructureGraph.with_empty_graph` / `with_local_env_strategy`** and the `MoleculeGraph` equivalents (materialsproject/pymatgen-core#103). This is fixed on main in #542, but so far only in pre-releases (e.g. 2026.8.28rc4). The `from_*` replacements already exist in pymatgen 2024.10.22, the current minimum in the requirements, so #542 does not need a new pymatgen floor.
   ```
   AttributeError: type object 'StructureGraph' has no attribute 'with_empty_graph'
   ```
2. **flask-caching >= 2.5.0 (released 2026-08-24) removed the lowercase cache-type aliases.** This is #544 and is *not* fixed yet, including in 2026.8.28rc4.
   ```
   ImportStringError: import_string() failed for 'flask_caching.backends.simple'.
   ```
   The fix is more than the one line in #544. Every lowercase `CACHE_TYPE` needs its class name:
   - `crystal_toolkit/core/plugin.py`: `"simple"` -> `"SimpleCache"`, and `"null"` -> `"NullCache"` (the `DEBUG_MODE` path breaks the same way)
   - `crystal_toolkit/apps/main.py`: `"null"` -> `"NullCache"` and `"redis"` -> `"RedisCache"`

   The class names also work on older flask-caching (`Cache(config={"CACHE_TYPE": "SimpleCache"})` and `"NullCache"` initialize on 2.2.0 and 2.4.1), so no new minimum version is needed.

A release with only #542 still breaks every structure display because of (2).

For now the tutorials pin to the following, which works with pymatgen 2026.9.24 on Python 3.12 and 3.14:
```
pip install "crystal-toolkit==2026.8.28rc4" "flask-caching<2.5"
```
I tested this by executing the pymatgen tutorial notebooks (https://github.com/computron/pymatgen_tutorials, Parts 1, 4, and 5; all structure and molecule displays render) and the structure display cell in https://github.com/computron/atomate2_tutorials Part 1. Once there is a release, I will switch both back to an unpinned install.

items.title: Telegram adapter silently degrades to Any stubs on ImportError, masking real failure
items.body:
**File:** `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py:236-276`

`except ImportError: TELEGRAM_AVAILABLE = False` sets every Telegram class (`Application`, `Bot`, `HTTPXRequest`, `TypeHandler`, etc.) to `typing.Any` as a fallback stub — but never logs *why* the import failed.

If `telegram` (python-telegram-bot) fails to import for a transient reason (e.g. a race between a gateway/service restart and a pip dependency sync still writing the package's `dist-info`/module files), the code doesn't fail fast. Instead it proceeds all the way to `Application.builder()...build()` / `HTTPXRequest(...)`, which then try to instantiate `Any`, producing:

```
ERROR hermes_plugins.telegram_platform.adapter: [Telegram] Failed to connect to Telegram: Any cannot be instantiated
```

This message gives zero indication of the real root cause (a swallowed `ImportError`), making it very hard to diagnose — especially since `TELEGRAM_AVAILABLE` is only checked later with a *different*, more helpful message ("python-telegram-bot not installed. Run: pip install python-telegram-bot") that never gets logged in this path because the import technically "succeeded" (bound everything to `Any`) rather than raising.

**Suggested fix:** log the original exception in the `except ImportError:` block, e.g.:

```python
except ImportError:
    logger.exception("[Telegram] python-telegram-bot import failed; platform will be unavailable")
    TELEGRAM_AVAILABLE = False
    ...
```

That would surface the actual traceback instead of the misleading downstream `Any cannot be instantiated` TypeError.

🤖 Filed via Claude Code after triaging a stale-checkout/gateway-restart incident where this exact race occurred.
